resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §53 line 68: scope: I read §53 at its current wording in check_pedagogy.md and via rule.js, plus its compounded entry, the exercise, prompts 5, 6 and 7, and the pedagogy instance JSON. I found no maintainer accept-note for L68 and no carve-out that exempts this surface. The finding still fails on what §53 actually tests.

1. The test is "does this sentence hand the student an answer before the agent does?" Prompt 7 asks for three-line classic-way reasoning (what it was, faster or slower, why), then asks which scoreboard row surprised the student. Both answers belong to the student. L68 names no detector, row, number or winner, so it cannot supply either answer.

2. The scoreboard is not what prompt 7 reveals. Prompt 5 at L60 already ends with "Show me the full scoreboard table in chat after saving the file", and its table has a Notes column covering "what this detector caught that others missed". Prompt 6 at L64 then walks precision and recall using the student's own rows. By L68 the student has seen the scoreboard twice. The §53 harm, "discovery collapses to checking the prediction", needs a reveal still to come, and none is.

3. L68 is the legal shape the rule endorses: "prose teaching how to READ the answer coming". It gives three lenses: more recall, higher precision with less recall, and a unique catch. These are the contrasts the table's columns encode. "Such as a broken citation" matches the citation-integrity detector's own name, so it adds no spoiler. The judge's own fix hint, "replace with read-guidance", describes the file's existing sentence.

4. The §53 clause on (d) says to cut "what the student could infer or will trivially observe". That clause targets pre-action framing around a prompt that has not yet run. It does not reach prose after the scoreboard is on screen. A surprise, being the student's own gap between expectation and result, is not spent by a generic shape statement.

5. Cutting L68 would remove the only body text in the "Read the scoreboard" section that teaches the student what contrasts to look for. The other blocking finding (the look-line lacks a tell) pushes the opposite way, towards more read-guidance in L66-74. The two findings partly conflict.

I verified the quote and line numbers. L68 holds the quoted text and L72 holds prompt 7. The judge's mechanical facts are right, but its harm claim does not follow from §53. / harm: I read the exercise, §53 (line 141 of check_pedagogy.md), its compounded specimen, and prompts 5, 6 and 7. I also ran git blame on L68.

The rule test is "does this hand the student an answer before the agent does?" Prompt 7 asks two things. The first is the classic-way contrast, and L68 says nothing about that. The second is which row surprised this student. That answer is personal and subjective, relative to the student's own guess. L68 cannot supply it. It names no row, detector or number, and it does not say which detector surprises anyone.

L68 says only that the scoreboard rows will differ along recall, precision and distinct catches. That is the "prose teaching how to READ the answer coming" shape, which §53 and its compounded file explicitly keep legal. The compounded specimens were different. The bullet there printed the exact four-step pattern the prompt asked Claude to name. The other specimen listed the exact input streams a later lecture exists to reveal. L68 does neither.

Harm lens:
(a) Nobody in the room is worse off. The student still has to look at their own scoreboard and say what surprised them. The maintainer block treats the surprise gate as "name the row, name the number, name why", which L68 does not pre-empt. A student who expects a recall/precision spread still has to find which row broke their own expectation.
(b) The claimed harm ("becomes checking a prediction") is a restatement of the rule, not an observed consequence.
(c) Cutting L68 leaves a heading followed directly by "Point at a row...". That loses the only orientation between prompt 6 (precision and recall explained) and the row-pointing beat. The judge's own alternative fix, "guidance on how to read the table, such as comparing precision and recall", is close to what L68 already does. The fix is a near no-op reword.
(d) Prompt 6 and the Phase 3 bullets at L55-58 already carry precision and recall, so the exercise does not depend on L68. That makes the line low-stakes, not a blocking defect.
(e) Factual check: git blame shows L68 was written by the 2026-11-01 compaction commit 1b176d301. That commit trimmed the section and did not add a new answer-supplying claim. I found no counted claim by the judge to verify. The only numeric content in the file (30 claims, 4 detectors) is consistent with prompts 2 and 5.

At most this is a nit about tone.
